hostedReviews.text: A lovely statue showing that two unstable adults, and be stabilized into one cohesive until when there’s a kid on the middle

hostedReviews.name: Galileo Broadway (Shubert Theatre)
hostedReviews.text: Galileo is a new show on Broadway, and while it wasn’t my favorite show that I’ve ever seen, I had a good time with the punky, more rock-inspired story of the astronomer.

hostedReviews.name: Hustle on George
hostedReviews.location: Ground Floor/403 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: Really good oat chai lattes, and some great brew coffee. This is one of the only coffee shops open at 5am, and this was just perfect for me.

hostedReviews.name: Hustlers.Syd
hostedReviews.location: LG, 24 York St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: I came to Hustlers. for a work event, and we ordered drinks and a whole variety of starters and entrees and everything was great. While this place is a bit on the higher end, the quality is certainly on the higher end as well.

hostedReviews.name: Mann med liten håndbevegelse
hostedReviews.text: People, walking, without their clothing. Like a nightmare you had that one time

hostedReviews.name: Edvard Grieg
hostedReviews.text: Grieg was an impressive composer, it’s even more impressive how much he accomplished without any elbows.

hostedReviews.name: Glory, glory with crutches
hostedReviews.text: Good art makes one feel something, and Glory certainly evokes a feeling

hostedReviews.name: National Monument for Victims of War 1940-45
hostedReviews.text: What exactly is going on here, and why does it represent what Norway did in the Second World War? It leaves one with a lot of questions

hostedReviews.name: Politihesten Tor
hostedReviews.text: Didn’t know that this horse was here and just stumbled upon it. A wonderful surprise

hostedReviews.name: Instalacja Jayco
hostedReviews.text: Geometric art which has a certain charm to it

hostedReviews.name: Statue of Franklin D. Roosevelt
hostedReviews.text: The American president is plopped atop the hill, with an eternally nice view, fit for a quadruple elected man.

hostedReviews.name: George C. Marshall
hostedReviews.text: Yes, evidently that is George C. Marshall stood at the base of the hill. Awkwardly out of the way, why is he here?

hostedReviews.name: Peter Jansen Wessel (Tordenskiold)
hostedReviews.text: Certainly a man that gives off pirate energy

hostedReviews.name: Scuba diver statue
hostedReviews.text: This statue sits ready to plunge into the water at any moment. It’s simply perfect for the pier

hostedReviews.name: Untuned Bell
hostedReviews.text: Very, very easy to miss at first. You can control the bell with a pedal on the ground.

hostedReviews.name: Rådhusplassen
hostedReviews.text: This pier is where you’ll catch some of the boat tours of the fjords. It’s also the back side of the stunning City Hall building, which has a nice view of the water. There’s also a number of statues around the area.

hostedReviews.name: Oslo City Hall
hostedReviews.text: Despite City Hall being closed when I visited, the building is just spectacular, and still well worth visiting. Each face is unique, with the best faces being the one from the water, and the one with the clock, in my opinion.

hostedReviews.name: Nordraaks plass
hostedReviews.text: Absolutely one of the coolest small parks in the city, if not the whole Nordics. There are giant dragon statues, chained up for our protection.

hostedReviews.name: Dronning Sonja
hostedReviews.text: For the Royal Funeral, all of the Royal statues across the country had flowers placed on them, but I don’t think anyone got more than Dronning Sonja. She was absolutely covered.

hostedReviews.name: Dronning Maud
hostedReviews.text: Not quite the most prominently featured statue in the Slottenspark, but Maud is located in one of the nicer wooded areas. Maud is depicted in the typical Norwegian style here.

hostedReviews.name: Karl Johan Monument
hostedReviews.text: Karl Johan sits high on his horse, towering above on a pedestal, facing the Palace. At the time of the Royal Funeral, the whole area was covered in flowers and flags in respect to the late King. …

hostedReviews.name: The Royal Palace
hostedReviews.text: Though the Palace is currently closed, there are still ceremonies held on the Palace grounds, which are open to the public. The Royal Funeral was held here, and the King lied in wake for a period prior.

hostedReviews.name: Slottsparken
hostedReviews.text: Slottsparken is the multiblock-sized park that surrounds the royal palace. There’s a pathway which has a series of modern art items along it, and a few more lined by trees. Royal ceremonies are held here, including the recent Royal Funeral (pictured)

hostedReviews.name: Aanerud Bakeri Oslo
hostedReviews.text: A small, lovely bakery. Aanerud Bakeri is located down a side street, a bit outside of downtown. The pastries were fantastic, you can skip the drip coffee.

hostedReviews.name: Oslo lufthavn
hostedReviews.text: A perfectly fine airport with a decent variety of lighter food options in the International terminal, and a broader selection in the Main terminal area. …

hostedReviews.name: Qantas International First Lounge Sydney
hostedReviews.location: Sydney Airport, Terminal 1 Departure Plaza, Mascot NSW 2020, Australia
hostedReviews.text: I stopped by the Qantas First Class Lounge one morning, and was treated like a princess. They made a great breakfast, which came out quickly, and then there were other areas to charge my devices and chill out before my flight

hostedReviews.name: Sydney Airport
hostedReviews.text: I quite enjoyed flying out of Sydney Airport. I was in First Class on American Airlines (for work) and the Qantas lounge was very phenomenal, I had such a good breakfast there. The rest of the airport had all of the amenities that you need.

hostedReviews.name: Menya City Japanese Noodle Bar
hostedReviews.text: I love Menya City; they’re quick, reasonably priced, and very tasty. The ramen was much better than the katsu.

hostedReviews.name: Google Sydney - One Darling Island
hostedReviews.location: 1 Darling Island Rd, Pyrmont NSW 2009, Australia
hostedReviews.text: I’ve visited this Sydney office twice now, and while it’s not the largest office, it does have its charm. The parking situation definitely doesn’t seem ideal for the people based out of here, but as a visitor that was no bother to me

hostedReviews.name: Life From A Suitcase
hostedReviews.text: Love the sentiment of the statue, and the execution is certainly fine as well

hostedReviews.name: Windjammers
hostedReviews.text: Ripping statue with a truly nautical view of the downtown skyline.

hostedReviews.name: Martin Place
hostedReviews.text: Sydney’s central business district is littered with giant, majestic, parliament-style buildings, and Martin Place is one of this set. Just stunning on its own, but somehow out of place in its current home

hostedReviews.name: Edward VII
hostedReviews.text: Edward VII is regally and royally presented on his horse. My main complaint with this statue is how hard it is to reach it, and how unfriend it is to pedestrians

hostedReviews.name: K H A O • S O I - カ オ • ソ ー イ
hostedReviews.location: Level 2/73-75 Liverpool St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: I love Khao Soi, it’s one of my favorite Thai dishes. I’ve been to Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand, where the dish comes from. While the Khao Soi here was fine, it was quite unique in a way that I didn’t love. I’ve never had one so spicy. I often love spice, but with Khao Soi’s pickled taste profile, it just wasn’t my favorite combo.

hostedReviews.name: Hyatt Regency Sydney
hostedReviews.text: Set right on Cockle Bay, the Hyatt Regency is a very nice business hotel. I’ve stayed here twice, and both times the rooms were quite large and well stocked. As always, I prefer a usable mini-fridge to one that’s trying to sell me products.

hostedReviews.name: Chinatown Sydney
hostedReviews.text: Chinatown doesn’t occupy that many blocks, but there is a very high density of business, and two arches to boot.

hostedReviews.name: Sydney Souvenirs
hostedReviews.location: PADDY’s MARKET Cnr Thomas &, Stall 460 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: In terms of vibes, Sydney Souvenirs’ was immaculate. No notes. And no comments on the products themselves.

hostedReviews.name: Golden Water Mouth
hostedReviews.text: I guess the tree carries some auspiciousness in bark, released by touch; but for the metal fencing, forbidding such an inquiry.

hostedReviews.name: Sydney's Water Features - Sydney Culture History Walks
hostedReviews.text: This one must’ve been under construction when I visited because it was all fenced off. I barely knew it was a monument

hostedReviews.name: Hay St Market
hostedReviews.location: Shop R1.05/13 Hay St, Haymarket NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: An indoor market comprised of a maze of restaurants, bakeries, bars, and coffee shops describes just a single portion of Hay St Market. Wander deeper and you’ll find more kitschy, touristy shops with more of a bazaar vibe. The place is way more expansive than one suspects.

hostedReviews.name: AG LEGO® Certified Store Sydney, Pitt St Mall – World’s Largest LEGO® Certified Store
hostedReviews.location: entry is Via, 400 George Street, Pitt Street Mall, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: This store claims to be the largest LEGO store in the world, and I find that a bit surprising, but sure it’s quite sizable and has a lot of the iconic brick company’s partnerships on display. It’s a fun place to stop while exploring the capital’s downtown.

hostedReviews.name: Royal Clock
hostedReviews.text: Queen Victoria Building has two impressive clocks, and the Royal Clock is the bulkier, more castle-resembling one. It’s got its charm, don’t get me wrong, but it’s definitely the lesser of the pair.

hostedReviews.name: Great Australian Clock
hostedReviews.text: There are two tiered clocks hanging from Queen Victoria Building and the Great Australian Clock appears to tell the story of the country/continent. The clock has so many details, the longer you inspect it, the more you get from it

hostedReviews.name: Queen Victoria Building
hostedReviews.text: The central business district of Syndey has a number of stunning, imperial buildings, and the Queen Victory stands alone as the singular best. From the glass panel on the windows, to the two giant, ornate clocks that hang in either hall, to the historical note in the top floor, this mall has a lot to see apart from the modern day stores.

hostedReviews.name: Athena
hostedReviews.text: Small, simple, and elegant, I really enjoyed this statue, and found its existence additive to the city’s beauty

hostedReviews.name: The Strand Arcade
hostedReviews.text: Sydney’s downtown should be known for its stunning buildings, and The Strand Arcade, one of many similar arcades, stands near the very top of the class. A tall, straight, singular hall with colorful, slanted, angular panels on the roof, and red carpeting and accenting provide a wonderful visual.

hostedReviews.name: Sydney Arcade
hostedReviews.text: There’s a few arcades (in the British sense, meaning a long covered building) in Sydney, but the eponymous one is definitely not the top one. Potentially the LEGO store is the most notable thing about this building, apart from the lovely building itself.

hostedReviews.name: Cenotaph
hostedReviews.text: Quite the beautiful monument, one of many in this area, which has an entire pedestrian-only street devoted to it. There were plentiful fresh wreaths when I visited, the area was extremely well kept

hostedReviews.name: Royal Australian Regiment Memorial
hostedReviews.location: Regimental Square, 339A George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: Not a giant monument, in stature, but still an impactful one. You’re just walking around the central business district and suddenly you stumble upon it

hostedReviews.name: Rabbit woman, Dogman, vespa and coffee
hostedReviews.location: Australia Square, 264 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: A lovely statue, a part of a series located in major cities around the work. It does appear that Rabbitwoman was originally holding something (maybe a coffee cup) which is now gone.

hostedReviews.name: Sirius Cannon
hostedReviews.text: This is actually a display in two parts: first the more obvious anchor, which is set off the ground, and then the cannon placed outwards, almost to intimidate oneself not to speak ill of the mediocre anchor

hostedReviews.name: Sirius Anchor
hostedReviews.text: Quite the large anchor is affixed onto a bit of ground, which itself is presented as a bit of art. Nah

hostedReviews.name: Thomas Sutcliff Mort
hostedReviews.text: Ol Tom is situated way up high, leaning on something of a pedestal as he gazes down on the masses

hostedReviews.name: Obelisk of Distances
hostedReviews.text: This obelisk almost taunts the reader in saying, “I bet you can’t make it to all of these far off locations”. And one day I hope to return to prove this monument wrong

hostedReviews.name: Principal Road Marker
hostedReviews.text: It’s a fine obelisk, and truly one of the finer monuments in Macquarie Place Park, but does an obelisk evoke roads? Maybe it’s a literal representation of a road

hostedReviews.name: Macquarie Place Park
hostedReviews.text: A very small park, but it rises above its smaller stature by being jam packed full of monuments, each fairly interesting in its own regard.

hostedReviews.name: Bonds of Friendship
hostedReviews.text: I did knot get this piece of art

hostedReviews.name: Second World War Servicewomen Memorial
hostedReviews.location: Jessie Street Gardens, 1-29 Loftus St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
hostedReviews.text: A statue recognizing the unsung and so oft unrecognized heroes of the second world war.

hostedReviews.name: Jessie Street Gardens
hostedReviews.text: The tiniest of greeneries, set entirely between giant skyscrapers, and filled with monuments. Jessie Street Gardens is many things, but hardly a garden (in the American sense)

hostedReviews.name: Moore Steps
hostedReviews.text: One of the staircases that’ll get you down to the water portion of Circular Quay. Nothing spectacular but it does get the job done.

hostedReviews.name: Dorothea Mackellar Writers Walk Plaque
hostedReviews.text: Quotes from famous Australians and visitors to the island continent are featured all around Circular Quay in circular golden plaques in the pavement

hostedReviews.name: Circular Quay Wharf
hostedReviews.text: The main waterfront area with the Opera House. It’s a great place to get some photos taken. Also, look down, as there’s a series of writers featured in little circles

hostedReviews.name: Tim Hortons
hostedReviews.location: 6301 Silver Dart Dr Terminal 1, Mississauga, ON L4V 1R9, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This Tim Hortons has a picture of Tim Horton in his hockey get-up. In decade of visiting the Tim Hortons chain, I never knew that it was named after a real guy.

hostedReviews.name: The Happy Tummy Bar & Grill
hostedReviews.text: A fine place for dinner, I had a bacon cheeseburger here and it was fine. I’d definitely come back and try the wings and poutine

hostedReviews.name: Yellowknife Liquor Store
hostedReviews.text: A very well stocked liquor store, with drinks from all over Canada and the world. I was especially appreciative that they carried nice ice wines from Niagara

hostedReviews.name: Raccine Park
hostedReviews.text: In the extremely flat Northwest Territories, Raccine Park contains something of a hill, which has been developed with a memorial

hostedReviews.name: Bush Pilots Monument
hostedReviews.location: 3513 Ingraham Dr #3511, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2E8, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The highest point in Old Town Yellowknife offering sweeping views from the lake to the rest of the city. It’s not too much of a hike to get up there, though it can get fairly icy and slippery

hostedReviews.name: Old Town Glassworks
hostedReviews.location: 3510 McDonald Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2H1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A lovely glass shop with tons of works made from recycled glasses. I also really appreciate the artwork and craftwork they had in the shop

hostedReviews.name: Wing Freak
hostedReviews.location: Nova Inn, 4401 Franklin Ave 3rd Floor, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1B5, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A decent lunch option, the chicken was well portioned, filling, and tasty. Wing Freak’s strangely located on the 3rd floor of the Nova Inn, but worth the awkward eye contact with the person in the lobby

hostedReviews.name: Yellowknife Visitor Centre
hostedReviews.location: Centre Square Mall, 5014 50 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R6, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This isn’t the nicest spot in downtown Yellowknife, but there’s information and free maps here. They’ll also give you a little pin and a certificate for crossing the 60th parallel

hostedReviews.name: ReLeaf NT
hostedReviews.text: A decent shop. Broad supply and reasonable prices, all that you need. They also gave me popcorn which was pretty sweet

hostedReviews.name: Yellowknife Public Library
hostedReviews.location: 2nd Floor, Centre Square Mall, 5022 49 St, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3R8, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The Library’s on the second floor of the mall, and features a small art collection with pieces around the floor. It’s a nice place to stop and support as a visitor

hostedReviews.name: Northern Souvenirs & Gifts
hostedReviews.text: A fair place to buy Canadian, Yellowknife, and Northwest Territory apparel and keepsakes. The store is very densely packed with goods

hostedReviews.name: Trader’s Grill
hostedReviews.text: Trader’s Grill is the restaurant within The Explorer Hotel, and it’s one of the nicest restaurants in Yellowknife. The Grilled Bison Ribeye was delicious and came with some nice sides. They also have Ice Wine for dessert. Trader’s has a …

hostedReviews.name: The Explorer Hotel
hostedReviews.text: I spent a single night at The Explorer Hotel, but I would stay long if I were in town for longer as everything was great: the restaurant, the rooms, the polar bear in the lobby - all of the essentials.

hostedReviews.name: Bristol Monument
hostedReviews.location: 361 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: One of the first things to greet you when you arrive in Yellowknife, the Bristol Monument sits high atop a hill above the welcome sign, with a brilliant and bright blue and red accented plane

hostedReviews.name: welcome yellowknife sign
hostedReviews.text: The Welcome Sign itself is pretty impressive, with the yellow knife and block text, how that pales in comparison to the large plane situated atop the hill next to it. All-in-all, this makes for one compelling stop

hostedReviews.name: Lakeshore Co-op Gas Bar
hostedReviews.location: 321 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This Co-op is located decently close to the airport if you’re returning a rental car. The shop is very well stocked

hostedReviews.name: Chan Lake Territorial Park
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0M0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: An moderate vista, which proves to be a fine place to stop, when you need some respite. I’ll add, this had some of the deepest snowbanks that I found

hostedReviews.name: Zhati Kue Friendship Centre
hostedReviews.text: A community center with some very friendly people inside

hostedReviews.name: Community Arbour
hostedReviews.text: When I showed up at the Arbour there wasn’t a soul to be found, however, there was a decently well kept fire, with fresh wood next to the hearth. I appreciate whoever left this warm treat, but wish they’d stuck around

hostedReviews.name: Our Lady of Providence
hostedReviews.location: DehCho Dr, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0A7, Canada
hostedReviews.text: An aesthetically crisp white church sat right on the water. It’s only open during the warmer months, so I can only assume the insulation isn’t the best

hostedReviews.name: Kakisa River Territorial Park
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A stunning valley, covered in a sheet of sparkling white, with a simple - and seldom tread - bridge spanning it

hostedReviews.name: Lady Evelyn Falls Territorial Park
hostedReviews.text: Completely inaccessible and covered in snow

hostedReviews.name: McNallie Creek Territorial Park Day Use Area
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Really spectacular looking falls when covered in snow. Nothing quite like those icicles dangling over the cliff

hostedReviews.name: Woodland Wok & Grill
hostedReviews.location: 66 Woodland Dr #8, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: For lunch, it seemed like the buffet was the only option, which I was ok with. They food was fine, very much mall Chinese food, similar to what I grew up eating in The States

hostedReviews.name: NWT Centennial Library
hostedReviews.location: 75 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This is one of the nicest places to stop in Hay River, the NWT Centennial Library really is a nexus for local information. They also had some interesting local papers that they let me keep as a souvenir

hostedReviews.name: Katlodeeche First Nation
hostedReviews.location: Hay River 1, Hay River, NT X0E, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Much easier to access in the months when the river is frozen. Just across the water from Hay River

hostedReviews.name: The Forks
hostedReviews.text: For half of the year, this portion of Hay River is frozen over, and it becomes an ice road connecting the two parts of the city across the water

hostedReviews.name: Marine Transportation Services - Shipyard
hostedReviews.location: 1 104 Ave, Hay River, NT X0E 0R2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: In the winter, the ships freeze into the harbor, and really have a nice visual from the beach

hostedReviews.name: Pumphouse Beach
hostedReviews.text: A peculiar place to visit in the colder months, as all that you can see (over the parking lot’s snowbank), is endless, nearly perfectly untouched snow. Cool vista, kinda windy, you can skip this one

hostedReviews.name: Parks Canada Fire Management Regional Fire Base
hostedReviews.text: Not a bad place to watch the northern lights (sadly, not seen, and thus not pictured); it’s nearly totally dark out here

hostedReviews.name: Town of Fort Smith
hostedReviews.location: 174 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: I spent a day in Fort Smith and had a really good time there! It’s a lovely little town nestled up at the eastern NWT/Alberta border. Visit Anna’s Restaurant, and get a coffee at Javapunks while you’re there

hostedReviews.name: Kaeser's Stores Ltd
hostedReviews.location: 76-80 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A very well-stocked supermarket for the remoteness of the city. I really appreciated that they carried Sap drinks

hostedReviews.name: Fort Smith Fire Dept
hostedReviews.location: 70 Breynat St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The temperature clocks in front of the Fire Dept display the power of the (sub-)Arctic sun. In March, as the sun is staying up for longer, the clock faces will span 20°C depending on how long they’ve been baking in the sun.

hostedReviews.name: Fort Smith Visitor Centre
hostedReviews.location: 149 McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The Visitor Centre was closed when I visited in March, and they appeared to be doing some reservations. I hope it’s nice when it reopens

hostedReviews.name: Wood Buffalo Inn
hostedReviews.text: Only stayed here for a single night, but the accommodations were great. The Inn is structured as a motel, but the rooms are stocked like entire apartments. If I come back to Fort Smith, I’ll definitely stay here again.

hostedReviews.name: Javapunks (Cafe)
hostedReviews.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Every town in the Northwest Territories has their cool coffee shop, and Javapunks is Fort Smith’s. They’ve got a decent drink coffee in a hip and cozy location. If I come back, I’d love to stay and do some work from here.

hostedReviews.name: NSIXTY Trading Company Ltd.
hostedReviews.location: 101 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: N60 Trading Company is a really interesting, well stocked hobby store. It’s such a gem for this kind of store to exist in such a remote location. I’m glad the people of the far north can get supplies for their hobbies, and games for the long and dark winters.

hostedReviews.name: Northern Life Museum & Cultural Centre and Gift Shop
hostedReviews.location: 110 King St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: I’m sad that I didn’t get to go into the Northern Life Museum, despite them claiming to be open. I even called them to no avail, a real shame

hostedReviews.name: Anna's Restaurant
hostedReviews.location: 338 Calder Ave, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Anna’s Restaurant was the only place that I ate while I was in Fort Smith, because after stopping in for brunch, I simply had to return for dinner to try the pizza (I got a calzone). Everything I had here was simply delicious, especially the incredible bread, and the towns were an absolute delight to talk to.

hostedReviews.name: Woodcutter's Monument
hostedReviews.text: Absolutely nothing to see in March, and a bit annoying to get to. Skip this one outside of summer

hostedReviews.name: Mountain Portage
hostedReviews.location: Unnamed Road, Wood Buffalo, AB T0P, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A bit harrowing to reach in winter, you’ll need to walk from the Portage Parking, marked on the map, with skis or snowmobiles also being options. The views truly aren’t the best, but hey, it’s something to see

hostedReviews.name: Mountain Portage Parking
hostedReviews.text: At least in winter, this is really as far as you’re going to want to drive. As a bonus for stopping here, you can get a bit of a view of the frozen water below. …

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to Fort Smith Sign
hostedReviews.location: McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A fine looking sign, for sure. People in town recommend coming out here, or to the airport, to get good pictures of the northern lights

hostedReviews.name: Tim Hortons
hostedReviews.location: 50 Trout St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Definitely the most remote Tim Hortons that I’ve visited. And on account of that remoteness, the selection is a bit more limited here than at some of the locations down south. If you show up in the mornings, there’s something of a line, but it moves fast.

hostedReviews.name: Little Buffalo River Falls Territorial Park
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: There are so few places between Hay River and Fort Smith, and even fewer which are open in the winter. Little Buffalo River Falls were open and generally accessible, though not the most impressive. Still worth stopping (but keep that engine running).

hostedReviews.name: Wood Buffalo National Park of Canada
hostedReviews.text: A wonderful place to go for a drive. But know, it’s very very sparse, with quite few people traversing the roads. During winter, play it safe and don’t stray too far off the main roads

hostedReviews.name: Big Buffalo River
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Big must be relative, and not to the region

hostedReviews.name: Pine Point Bridge
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R7, Canada
hostedReviews.text: In a land of sparseness, everything is notable, and this bridge was lovely, vibrant hue of green, and gave some interesting views during wintertime

hostedReviews.name: Esso
hostedReviews.location: 921 MacKenzie Hwy Ss 22, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A full service gas station with some decently reasonable prices. Because it’s located on the main road, it’s easy to stop here just before leaving town

hostedReviews.name: Georginas Place Thrift Shop
hostedReviews.location: 69 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A small, well stocked thrift shop located in what feels like a house

hostedReviews.name: Hay River Tourist Information
hostedReviews.location: McBryan Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: While the center was shut when I came by in late March, they did have some of the finest art in the region on display just outside, and that was plenty for me

hostedReviews.name: Rat Lake
hostedReviews.location: Rat Lake, MacKenzie County, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Completely inaccessible from Indian Cabins, sadly

hostedReviews.name: Indian Cabins Trading Post
hostedReviews.location: Hwy 35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: As you head south from the 60th Parallel by Hay River, Indian Cabins Trading Post is the first thing that you’ll hit south of the border. And what a wonderful place to stop, if only for Screw Stewie, a dog that’s all too excited to meet you

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to the Northwest Territories Sign
hostedReviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: In terms of border signs, this one is quite impressive, especially when compared to its contemporaries - the Welcome to Alberta sign opposite it and the signs by Fort Smith. The whole place is a ghost town if you make the journey in winter, with the exception of the odd car flying by

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to Mackenzie County Sign
hostedReviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Much better than the Alberta sign a hundred meters in front of it. You got a sun and everything on the sign, it’s doing its own thing

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to Alberta Sign
hostedReviews.location: AB-35, Meander River, AB T0H 2P0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Albertans, let’s be honest. This sign isn’t bringing your province the glory that it deserves. You gotta dream bigger, especially when the NWT sign opposite yours is so much bigger and nicer

hostedReviews.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park
hostedReviews.location: Mackenzie Hwy, Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: If you’re looking to see the inside of any of the buildings, I’d recommend visiting in the summer months

hostedReviews.name: Sixtieth Parallel Territorial Park Visitor Centre
hostedReviews.location: Hwy 1, South Slave Region, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Rating this on aesthetics alone, as the whole place was shut for winter when I visited in late March. With pristine, untouched snow, and tall ordinary trees surrounding the simple structure, the aesthetic was fine

hostedReviews.name: Alexandra Falls Observation Deck
hostedReviews.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This deck is situated out on the cliff face, above the falls, giving a sweeping view of Alexandra Falls and the lower river basin

hostedReviews.name: Alexandra Falls
hostedReviews.location: 1 Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 1G3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Completely frozen in the winter, the Alexandra Falls make for a memorable visit regardless of the time of the year

hostedReviews.name: Alexandra Falls Territorial Park Day Use Area
hostedReviews.location: Rte Waterfalls, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: One of the few stops along the NWT Highways which was actually open and accessible during the winter. The trail was mostly packed snow leading to the observation pavilion.

hostedReviews.name: Big Lake
hostedReviews.location: 2-4 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Big Lake is the only real coffee shop in Hay River, and they make a decent cup of coffee and muffin. They also have more full meals, and for more meals than breakfast, but I never tried either; maybe my loss.

hostedReviews.name: Hay River Public Beach
hostedReviews.text: I came here to watch a sunrise in March, and it was -39°, the coldest temperature that I felt in the subarctic. It’s a nice place to take in the rising winter sun, but it can get seriously cold here, being exposed to the lake air.

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to Enterprise Sign
hostedReviews.text: Simple sign, could be a bit more fantabulous

hostedReviews.name: Hay River Inukshuk
hostedReviews.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The Inukshuk is stood in front of the Fire Department, between the Canadian and Northwestern Territories flags, looking imposing as you drive into downtown Hay River. Quite a sight to behold

hostedReviews.name: Hay River Fire Department
hostedReviews.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: One of the more beautiful structures in Hay River, especially at dusk

hostedReviews.name: Northmart
hostedReviews.location: 81 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A very large store, in the historic and general sense, which has whatever you need. My main complaint is how early they close (6pm) as there were multiple times when I wanted a late night snack to no avail

hostedReviews.name: Doghouse pub
hostedReviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: I visited the Keys Lounge a few times before I decided to try the Doghouse Pub (they share a menu, including the bar options), and wow, as a solo diner I had a much better time eating at the bar. If you’re planning to eat alone, go in the back entrance and eat in The Doghouse at the bar.

hostedReviews.name: Keys Dining Lounge & Restaurant
hostedReviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Keys Dining Lounge is located within the Ptarmigan Inn, and is most likely the nicest restaurant within 3hrs of Hay River. I came here a few times and really enjoyed the Poutine, Ribs, Wings, and the Burger (which also supports charity). …

hostedReviews.name: Ptarmigan Inn
hostedReviews.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Whether you’re staying at the Ptarmigan Inn or not, they have one of the best restaurants in town (Keys Lounge) and one of the best bars in the surrounding 6hrs (Doghouse Pub). It’s a nice place to stop while you’re in town

hostedReviews.name: Riverview Cineplex
hostedReviews.location: 25 Studney Dr, Enterprise, NT X0E 0R1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: With Yellowknife’s movie theatre now being shut, this may be the last cinema in the NWT. Sadly I couldn’t support them, I hope they survive and keep fighting the good fight

hostedReviews.name: Ring's Pharmacy Ltd
hostedReviews.location: 6 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 0A9, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A fairly full pharmacy and convenience store for the remoteness of the region

hostedReviews.name: Town of Hay River
hostedReviews.location: 62 Woodland Dr #100, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: While it doesn’t necessarily have the best reputation among locals across the NWT, I enjoyed my days in Hay River. There’s a few hotels, a couple good restaurants, a coffee shop, and everything else you need to survive up here. Hay River is a fine place to visit

hostedReviews.name: Cambridge Executive Suites
hostedReviews.location: 31 Capital Dr #101, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: I really did enjoy staying at the Cambridge Executive Suites, and like the people that own it, but when they only clean with a broom and dustpan, they leave a lot of hair in the rooms. Otherwise, the apartments are wonderful, but they need to invest in a vacuum

hostedReviews.name: Town welcome sign
hostedReviews.location: Q5VJ+8C, Hay River, NT X0E 1G5, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Hey, it is a beautiful sign. You wanna stop and take it in on the way into town.

hostedReviews.name: Junction of Highways 1 and 2
hostedReviews.text: You’d think that there’d be more here, but in winter, this area was exceptionally dead except for the trucks passing by. Whether you’re going to/from Fort Smith, Hay River, or Yellowknife, you’ll be passing through Enterprise which is entirely comprised by this intersection.

hostedReviews.name: Information Board
hostedReviews.location: Fort Smith, Unorganized, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This information board is located at the intersection of Route 1 and Route 3, as 3 dead-ends into 1. It’s a fine board, I guess it’s something to note

hostedReviews.name: Deh Cho Bridge
hostedReviews.location: South Slave Region, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The Northwest Territories is so sparse of human creations that any are notable. Arguably, the Deh Cho Bridge is the most spectacular landmark outside of the few cities of the NWT, with a stark prominence visible from miles away on either …

hostedReviews.name: Big River Service Centre LP
hostedReviews.location: 1 NT-3 Lot 3, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0L0, Canada
hostedReviews.text: One of the better places to stop on the route connecting Hay River and Yellowknife, with reasonably priced gas and some hot food, snacks, and drinks. If you’ve got the time, stop off in Fort Providence

hostedReviews.name: Snowshoe Inn Cafe & Craft Shop
hostedReviews.location: Mackenzie Drive, Fort Providence, NT X0E 0A7, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A must stop location if you’re driving from Hay River to Yellowknife or visa-versa. Great options for either breakfast or lunch, and some nice coffee with two brews to choose from. They also have a little shop next door with arts and crafts that they’ll open if you ask

hostedReviews.name: North Arm Territorial Park Day Use Area
hostedReviews.text: In the winter, the lake is entirely frozen over, so you’ll see a person or two camping in a car in the parking lot, and the lake is otherwise untouched. It’s a beautiful sight to be seen and it nearly looks like the moon or mars

hostedReviews.name: Frank Channel Bridge
hostedReviews.text: In a land nearly untouched by man, a single and simple bridge becomes all too notable. The Frank Channel Bridge was under construction when I passed across it in March, and there was a street light enforcing the single lane of traffic.

hostedReviews.name: Miss Saigon
hostedReviews.location: Inside Kim’s Confectionary, 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1E3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Miss Saigon is an absolutely delicious takeout option just a few blocks outside of downtown Yellowknife. Located inside of Kim’s Confectionery, this unassuming location doesn’t have the best aesthetics, but makes some delicious Vietnamese food with great portions for a low cost

hostedReviews.name: Kim's Confectionary
hostedReviews.location: 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A slightly smaller convenience store, but they carry a variety of more snacky options, and a few more packaged staples. Miss Saigon’s is located inside of Kim’s, and is great!

hostedReviews.name: Dettah Ice Road
hostedReviews.location: School Draw Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3G2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: It’s less of a singular road (at the Yellowknife portion) and more of a, people drive on the lake to go where they need to. Multiple entrances and multiple exits, but with one major artery heading further into the lake.

hostedReviews.name: Snowkings' Winter Festival
hostedReviews.location: 1 Kingsway, Yellowknife Bay, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This year was the 31st anniversary of Snowkings’ Winter Festival, in which they build an expansive ice castle on the frozen lake, with an ice carving contest situated outside. It’s a truly impressive endeavor, executed to an excellent …

hostedReviews.name: Gallery of the Midnight Sun
hostedReviews.location: 5005 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A gallery with a variety of local crafts and taxidermies, including a number of beautiful, more premium art pieces. It’s nice to walk through this gallery regardless of whether you intend to buy anything.

hostedReviews.name: Down to Earth Gallery
hostedReviews.location: 5007 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A lovely little gallery and local craft and art shop, which is packed full of goodies. The location is located inside of a log cabin ordained with local art

hostedReviews.name: NWT Brewing Company / The Woodyard Brewhouse & Eatery
hostedReviews.location: 3905 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2S6, Canada
hostedReviews.text: If you have some spare time in Yellowknife, plop yourself down at the bar at NWT Brewing and you’ll discover a number of great local beers, and equally great local people. They brew a beer each year for the Snowkings Ice Festival, on the lake next door, each winter.

hostedReviews.name: Aurora Emporium Art Gallery
hostedReviews.location: 4701 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The owner is a longtime Yellowknifer who sells a number of local crafts, perfect for gifts down south. They’ll also print your pictures on mugs, especially ones of northern lights.

hostedReviews.name: Centre Square Mall
hostedReviews.text: One of the most prominent buildings in downtown Yellowknife, and while it may not be as thriving as it once was, evidenced by a lot of people standing around and a whole section being closed off. Still, they have a Tim Hortons, a nice Visitor Centre with mementos for tourists, and a decent library. If you’re in YK, stop by

hostedReviews.name: Barren Ground Coffee
hostedReviews.text: Really delicious coffee, roasted locally in the NWT. Love supporting a local business, especially when the drip coffee is so good.

hostedReviews.name: Houcine's Your Independent Grocer Yellowknife 50th Ave
hostedReviews.location: 4802 Franklin Ave #14, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1C4, Canada
hostedReviews.text: A very full supermarket, with slightly higher prices, though nothing unreasonable considering the remoteness of the location. If you’re visiting Yellowknife from another country, there’s a few Canadian touristic products for you to buy as gift or souvenirs

hostedReviews.name: YK Centre Clock
hostedReviews.text: If you give me a clock, I’m going to need to take a picture with the high score, or rather the low score in this case. It was -32° here, but -39° on the trip (Hay River Beach at sunrise)

hostedReviews.name: United Nations Tank Display
hostedReviews.text: You seriously don’t expect to see a UN Tank in Canada, but this one appears to have been abandoned here, and was fully covered in snow when I visited

hostedReviews.name: Legislative Assembly of the Northwest Territories
hostedReviews.location: 4570 48 St, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3A5, Canada
hostedReviews.text: One of the more impressive city hall buildings that I’ve ever seen in my travels, as there’s a giant polar bear skin laying on the floor intimidatingly, and a huge Zinc wall behind the main dais

hostedReviews.name: North of 60° Mining Memorial
hostedReviews.text: A fairly simple monument, but an elegant looking one at that. May they rest in Peace, indeed

hostedReviews.name: Museum Restaurant by Sundog
hostedReviews.text: I visited the Heritage Centre first thing in the morning, before I’d eaten breakfast, and so I stopped at Sundog more out of convenience than intention. Regardless, I really enjoyed the breakfast sandwich and potatoes that I had here.

hostedReviews.name: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre
hostedReviews.text: One of my favorite attractions in Yellowknife, and the larger NWT, this museum both tells the history of the region and the historical people, and displays a lot of art and culture of the locals that call this far northern region home. …

hostedReviews.name: Ceremonial Circle
hostedReviews.text: An attraction, of sorts. There’s a pathway of all the regional flags connecting City Hall from the Heritage Center and Legislative Assembly, along the body of water

hostedReviews.name: United in Celebration sculpture
hostedReviews.location: Sombe K'e Civic Plaza, 4910 52 St, Yellowknife, NT X0E, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This sculpture depicts two people dancing in shadow with shields (?) in their hands, and is situated right at the water’s edge, though in winter it’s a bit hard to tell.

hostedReviews.name: Somba K'e Civic Plaza
hostedReviews.text: In wintertime, there’s not a ton here, but for a large tree and the United in Celebration sculpture, and a ton of wind and cold

hostedReviews.name: Yellowknife City Hall
hostedReviews.text: While the building was closed when I visited (on a Sunday morning), I did enjoy exploring the surrounding area and its sparse art. If you’re hoping to use the building to warm up, plan to go elsewhere

hostedReviews.name: Javaroma Gourmet Coffee & Tea
hostedReviews.location: 5201 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3S9, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Javaroma is the (only) Yellowknife local chain, with a few locations scattered around the northern capital city. The coffee isn’t incredible, as is typical with most chains, but I really appreciate that they opened early on the weekends. They also had some fancy looking pastries

hostedReviews.name: Budget Car & Truck Rental
hostedReviews.location: 20 Airport Road, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: Don’t be afraid of the slightly scary sign posted outside of the closed airport location, someone most likely is on the way to meet you at your reservation time. …

hostedReviews.name: Yellowknife Airport
hostedReviews.location: 100 Idaa Rd, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3T2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: In terms of tiny airports in remote places of the globe, Yellowknife Airport is decently well equipped and serviced! I also believe that this is the only airport with a life sized polar bear in the main terminal, but I’ll have to keep …

hostedReviews.name: Tim Hortons
hostedReviews.location: Pearson International Airport - T1 Domestic Post Security - Near, Gate D42, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: This Tim Hortons had a decent selection at 8pm, with nearly all of the donut bins remaining full. Just what I needed on a quick stopover

hostedReviews.name: Plaza Premium Lounge Toronto Pearson (US Transborder, Terminal 1)
hostedReviews.location: Toronto Pearson Int'l Airport, Gate E77, International Departures, Terminal 1, Mississauga, ON L4V 1R9, Canada
hostedReviews.text: There’s two Plaza Premium Lounges in the Toronto Airport, and they both take Priority Pass. Neither is very good, and this is the worse of the two. The food really isn’t great, and it’s often quite crowded where you’re waiting for a while …

hostedReviews.name: Plaza Premium Lounge Toronto Pearson (Domestic Departures, Terminal 1)
hostedReviews.location: Toronto Pearson International Airport, Right After Security, Domestic Departures, Level 3, 6301 Silver Dart Dr Terminal 1 Departures, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: There’s two Plaza Premium Lounges in the Toronto Airport. They book take Priority Pass, and neither is really very good, but this is the better of the two. The food isn’t great, nor is the drink selection. Make sure not to lose your ticket, and they circulate and check tickets to make sure that no one overstays their visit.

hostedReviews.name: Toronto Pearson Int'l Airport
hostedReviews.location: 6301 Silver Dart Dr, Mississauga, ON L5P 1B2, Canada
hostedReviews.text: The Toronto Airport will be your launchpad if you’re flying from the eastern side of the United States, and are trying to go to northern Canada, as this was the easiest way for me to get to Yellowknife. …

hostedReviews.name: ARCO
hostedReviews.text: By far the cheapest gas around Haight/Divisidaro area, and they have working mobile payment readers on the pumps. …

hostedReviews.name: Dunkin'
hostedReviews.location: 30th & Market St Station Amtrak Food Court, Philadelphia, PA 19104
hostedReviews.text: This is the Dunkin’ in the main hall, and there’s actually a second, less crowded one, near the SEPTA Regional Rails. America Runs on Dunkin’ especially when it’s the only option in the train hall (but for a Pret down the hall).

hostedReviews.name: Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club New York City LGA
hostedReviews.location: LaGuardia Airport, Terminal B, Level 1A, East Elmhurst, NY 11371
hostedReviews.text: The Chase Sapphire Lounge is a Priority Pass app (at least for people who have it through a Chase credit card), and operates by a QR code and website system for food ordering, but there’s also smaller dishes available at counters around the room, a full bar, and a smattering of drink fridges and snack jars.

hostedReviews.name: Wawa
hostedReviews.text: A very convenient Wawa location, with a large gas station and a full store.

hostedReviews.name: Chickie's & Pete's Terminal A
hostedReviews.text: Airport Terminal location of a classic Philly area restaurant known for their Crab Fries. They have nearly their whole menu here, with a decent beer selection. I appreciated that they had a quick togo option as well

hostedReviews.name: Ashley's Restaurant and Bar
hostedReviews.location: 68 W Baltimore Pike, Glen Mills, PA 19342
hostedReviews.text: Ashley’s is a neighborhood bar and restaurant with an extensive salad bar and good pasta and burgers. I’ve been here a few times, and everything that I’ve ordered has been pretty consistently solid.

hostedReviews.name: AMC DINE-IN Painters Crossing 9
hostedReviews.text: One of the dine-in AMC Theatres, which will still sell you popcorn, pretzels, and the classic movie snacks and drinks, but they also have a fuller food and drink menu which they’ll deliver to your seat. …

hostedReviews.name: Target
hostedReviews.location: 500 N Congress Ave, Lake Park, FL 33403
hostedReviews.text: Got there right after they opened and the place went quite empty and quiet. No issues to report, it’s a big store

hostedReviews.name: Delco's Original Steaks & Hoagies
hostedReviews.text: My local home cheesesteak spot, they’ve got a good sandwich, with some Amoroso-style bread. Their medium is huge, I can barely finish it when I’m famished. A large would feel a small family, I would assume.

hostedReviews.name: Bread and Butter Kitchen
hostedReviews.text: A decent and slightly more reasonably priced lunch option, potentially on account of it being a peninsula away from downtown Annapolis. The omelettes were decent, though nothing was too memorable

hostedReviews.name: Love & Honey Fried Chicken
hostedReviews.text: Really tasty chicken tenders, and a great portion for the cost. They drizzle honey atop, which is just such a great topper

hostedReviews.name: WhatSub Sub Shop Palm Beach Gardens
hostedReviews.location: 10800 N Military Trl #120, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
hostedReviews.text: WhatSub has a selection of Cold and Hot Sandwiches which all seemed to really be quite sizable. I ordered the Chicken Parm, and it had a ton of Chicken on it, served on some great bread

hostedReviews.name: Oceana Coffee Drive Thru
hostedReviews.text: Oceana has some decent drip coffee for a fair price. While they have a fairly well sized interior, they also have a drive through as well

hostedReviews.name: Lingonberry (Northlake)
hostedReviews.location: 4258 Northlake Blvd, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
hostedReviews.text: Really solid drip coffee for a reasonable price

hostedReviews.name: Sancho Pistola's
hostedReviews.text: Burritos aren’t huge, and are a bit on the pricier side for the area, but they are very tasty.

hostedReviews.name: Impresso Express
hostedReviews.location: 544 E Girard Ave Storefront, Philadelphia, PA 19125
hostedReviews.text: The drip coffee is ok!

hostedReviews.name: JD Vance Mural
hostedReviews.text: It’s hideous, it’s perfect. I love it, the eyes followed me my whole walk home, and may still be following me now

hostedReviews.name: Front Street Walls
hostedReviews.text: Beautiful, story-tall murals lining Front Street, under the El

hostedReviews.name: Mecha Noodle Bar
hostedReviews.location: 1700 N Front St Ste 2.1, Philadelphia, PA 19122
hostedReviews.text: Mecha makes a decent pho, in a trendy and aesthetically pleasing bar / restaurant space. The Happy Hour specials look decent as well

hostedReviews.name: AMC Broadstreet 7
hostedReviews.text: Certainly on the smaller end for urban AMCs, Broadstreet has a single concession counter, and all of the theatres are all located along a long hallway. That being said, it’s a perfectly lovely place to watch movies.

hostedReviews.name: Sumalee Thai
hostedReviews.text: I ordered Chicken Pad Thai delivery from here, and it was extremely meh.

hostedReviews.name: Loco Pez
hostedReviews.text: Loco Pez makes a pretty good burrito, which made for a really sizable lunch

hostedReviews.name: Rowhome Coffee - Front Street
hostedReviews.text: Rowhome Coffee makes their Breakfast Sandwiches on Pretzels! How ingenious! The Sausage, Egg, and Cheese ones were delicious and served piping hot. The coffee was fine

hostedReviews.name: Fishtown Beverage
hostedReviews.text: Fishtown Beverage may not have the most square footage, but they occupy the space that they have quite well. That includes a really sizable refrigerated section.

hostedReviews.name: Wawa
hostedReviews.text: This Wawa is perfectly fine. They have the normal menu and selection, and they have a perfectly fine gas station, but their ordering is very slow, and they forget about online orders. Make sure to check in often to make sure they’re working on your food and/or drinks.

hostedReviews.name: Gilda
hostedReviews.text: Gilda is a small coffee shop and bakery, but wow do they pack a mighty punch. You can get a drip coffee to stay, and they’ll give you refills, and the pastries are simply out-of-this-world. I’ll have to come back and try the rest of the menu.

hostedReviews.name: ReAnimator Coffee - Fishtown
hostedReviews.text: ReAnimator’s a neighborhood coffee spot, but with its central location, it really serves as the hub/heart of the local neighborhood. I like their drip coffee

hostedReviews.name: PrimoHoagies
hostedReviews.text: PrimoHoagies are a great option for a quick and convenient lunch. You can order ahead on their website, and then go pick it up when it’s done, typically in 10mins. I really like their Italian Hoagie.

hostedReviews.name: Caletta
hostedReviews.text: Caletta is the bar area of Bastia / Hotel Anna and Bel, and it’s an intimate, lovely spot to stop for a more elevated drink and snack inside of the fancy hotel. …

hostedReviews.name: Philly Halal Gyro
hostedReviews.location: Aramingo Avenue &, E York St, Philadelphia, PA 19125
hostedReviews.text: An extremely reasonably priced food truck, serving Halal Food. I liked the Chicken Over Rice, but it was a bit heavy on the hot sauce. I’ll go a bit lighter next time, and may try another meat.

hostedReviews.name: Pet Supplies Plus Fishtown
hostedReviews.text: A very well-stocked pet store, with the largest section catering to dogs, followed by cats, and finally fish. I just wish the cat section were a bit larger.

hostedReviews.name: The Richmond Shops IGA
hostedReviews.text: A neighborhood grocer with a decent selection of fresh produce, meat, and baked goods. They got all of the national brands, as well as a number of store brands, across products

hostedReviews.name: Manhasset
hostedReviews.text: This LIRR station has a nice indoor portion which provides places to sit down, and to provide some shelter from the elements

hostedReviews.name: Tom Seaver Statue
hostedReviews.text: The statue is situated directly in front of the main facade of the stadium, so it’s easy to frame it in your best shots of the complex

hostedReviews.name: Sammy's Woodfired Pizza
hostedReviews.location: Terminal 4, 1 World Wy, Los Angeles, CA 90045
hostedReviews.text: I came here for breakfast, and ordered the breakfast sandwich with potatoes, and while it was very pricey, it was all delicious and exactly what my body needed.

hostedReviews.name: AmericanAirlinesFlagshipLounge
hostedReviews.text: A very nice First Class lounge, don’t get me wrong, but the food was all very fancy, and not at all what I wanted after flying for 15hrs, so I brought in food from downstairs, which they were totally fine with.

hostedReviews.name: Qantas International First Lounge Los Angeles
hostedReviews.text: This lounge functions more as a sit down restaurant, where you may need to wait for a table. Not the best snacks outside of the dining area

hostedReviews.name: Chelsea Lounge JFK - British Airways & American
hostedReviews.location: JFK Terminal 8, Central Terminal Area, JFK International Airport, NY 11430
hostedReviews.text: The Chelsea Lounge in JFK is the First Class lounge that services American and British Airways passengers. These lounges are uber luxurious, and have a menu full of delicacies. While they didn’t have the Steak Frites, I didn’t so enjoy the Tartare and Pappardelle before my cross country flight.

hostedReviews.name: Pennsylvania Railroad World War II Memorial
hostedReviews.location: William H. Gray III 30th Street Station, 2955 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104
hostedReviews.text: The signature artwork of 30th St: a humongous statue of an angel holding a fallen man on a pedestal, lined with the names of the fallen.

hostedReviews.name: Amtrak Philadelphia Train Station
hostedReviews.text: 30th St Station serves both Amtrak and SEPTA, and thus serves as Southeastern PA’s main connector to the region and to the whole Mid-Atlantic area. …

hostedReviews.name: MOD Pizza
hostedReviews.location: 1751 Wilmington Pike Ste F-1, Glen Mills, PA 19342
hostedReviews.text: A good place to get a fairly quick and decently cheap, fully customizable pizza. It’s the kind of pie that doesn’t age the best, so eat it quickly

hostedReviews.name: Margaret Kuo's Kitchen
hostedReviews.location: 1109 W Baltimore Pike Suite A, Media, PA 19063
hostedReviews.text: Margaret Kuo has long been a quality restaurant chain in the Philly area, and I was happy to find that was still true in the 2020s. Had a great dinner at the Granite Run location, with a variety of Chinese and Pan-Asian dishes. Love that they bring out peanuts and cucumbers as free appetizers.

hostedReviews.name: Meghan's
hostedReviews.text: Meghan’s is a staple of Concord Township, as its beloved greasy spoon diner. While they’re often full, it never takes too long for a table to open up. …

hostedReviews.name: Dock Bridge
hostedReviews.location: Passaic River, Harrison NJ, Harrison, NJ 07029
hostedReviews.text: The Dock Bridge is the railway bridge which crosses the Passaic River. It’s pretty rusted over, and something of an eyesore, but it’s got its charm

hostedReviews.name: Sheetz
hostedReviews.text: Now I’m a Wawa guy, so I’m coming in here with a slant, but the main problem with Sheetz is the speed. When you have a basic order, like a simple breakfast sandwich, you want them ready to go. At Sheetz they actually brag about the fact that they making things to order, which is obscenely slow at most locations, including this one.

hostedReviews.name: The Pied Piper of Bedford County
hostedReviews.text: I wasn’t expecting this funny little guy, when I was driving east across Pennsylvania, but life exists to delight, I suppose. What is his story, where is he from, what secrets does he keep?

hostedReviews.name: Lookout Point Mt. Ararat
hostedReviews.text: If you stop at the Flight 93 Memorial on the way from Pittsburgh back east, you’ll be driving across Mt. Ararat. You owe it to yourself to stop and take in the vista for a moment.

hostedReviews.name: Scenic Overlook
hostedReviews.text: It’s quite the vista, Mt. Ararat. It almost makes me feel like I’m back in the hills of Napa county

hostedReviews.name: Post-9/11 U.S. Armed Forces Memorial at Patriot Park
hostedReviews.text: This is an accompanying Memorial, across the street from the official Flight 93 Memorial, this one with flags and the shadow of a person kneeling at a soldier’s memorial. There were only a few flags laid out, far fewer than I was anticipating.

hostedReviews.name: Memorial Plaza
hostedReviews.text: The Memorial Plaza is located at the end of a long walkway from the Visitor Shelter, and consists of a large wavy cement wall with the names of the deceased on it. It’s really a touching tribute, where the walk gives you time to reflect.

hostedReviews.name: Flight 93 National Memorial - Visitor Center
hostedReviews.text: The Flight 93 Visitor Center itself is perched up on a hill overlooking the disaster’s field, which is now the Memorial Plaza today. The building itself is truly a piece of art, made of simple concrete and glass walls. Unfortunately the architecture functions like something of a wind tunnel so it can get very cold inside.

hostedReviews.name: Flight 93 National Memorial
hostedReviews.text:
A touching memorial to the Flight 93 tragedy that occurred on September 11th. There are multiple buildings that encompass the memorial, in some
ways recognizing the field that was scattered here. There’s also a giant wind chime on the way in, in a stunning tower.

hostedReviews.name: YINZ Coffee Friendship
hostedReviews.text: Decent coffee, great best, incredible name

hostedReviews.name: Shibam Coffee
hostedReviews.text: Very cool aesthetics, and interesting sounding drinks, but I really didn’t enjoy what I got.

hostedReviews.name: Pamela's | P&G Diner
hostedReviews.text: Pamela’s is a Pittsburgh institution, and their hotcakes are renowned. They’re like crepes, almost, and you can get them filled with fruit and cream. I always get The Morning After breakfast special, and substitute in Specialty Hot Cakes …

hostedReviews.name: Morrow Park
hostedReviews.text: Less a park, and more a statue with some grass, Morrow Park isn’t much to write home about, not to denigrate the perfectly fine statue at its heart.

hostedReviews.name: FET-FISK restaurant + bar
hostedReviews.text: Didn’t have a reservation and queued up with a party of 5 about 10 minutes before they opened and got seated at the bar. Fet-Fisk is a very cool upscale restaurant with a variety of excellent seafood and meat options. I had the Tartar, the …

hostedReviews.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
hostedReviews.text: Phipps Conservatory is an outstandingly beautiful building, filled with a variety of plants from around the world. However, the most notable thing about this museum isn’t alive, and is entirely Silicon-based. The glass structure of the …

hostedReviews.name: Flag Monument
hostedReviews.text: A very simple monument, with a large, gravestone-esque rock and a lone flag on a flagpole. The monument recognizes America on its 150th birthday, and now at year 250, it’s been here for a century.

hostedReviews.name: Scotty Dog Statue
hostedReviews.location: University Center, 5032 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
hostedReviews.text: This statue is new (since I graduated), and I’m not certain how I feel about it. It’s a fine statue, sure, but does it belong in front of the UC? Put it in front of the admissions building

hostedReviews.name: Flagstaff Hill
hostedReviews.text: Flagstaff Hill is the far north portion of Schenley Park, which connects Phipps Conservatory with Carnegie Mellon’s campus. It’s a lovely place to sit, and a convenient place to cut across to get to Oakland.

hostedReviews.name: Newell-Simon Hall
hostedReviews.text: Newell-Simon Hall is one of the Robots centers on campus, and the building is dressed accordingly. For the last fifteen (plus) years, Tank the Robo-Receptionist has greeted you, and there’s occasionally robotics displays on the first floor. …

hostedReviews.name: The Mall
hostedReviews.text: There are two interconnected green lawns on Carnegie Mellon’s main campus: The Cut, extending to Forbes, and The Mall, with its iconic shot extended out to Pitt’s Cathedral of Learning.

hostedReviews.name: The Fence
hostedReviews.text: The most iconic landmark on Carnegie Mellon’s campus. The Fence has strict rules, it can only be painted by hand and by brush (no rollers), and it can only be painted after midnight. To hold The Fence, you need to keep two (or more) people …

hostedReviews.name: The Bride of Penn Ave
hostedReviews.text: A hauntingly beautiful painting of the Penn Ave of Pittsburgh yester. Maybe we’ll get back there one day

hostedReviews.name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
hostedReviews.text: Pittsburgh Glass Center is a combination studio space and teaching studio, where you can take classes to learn the craft of glassblowing. The studio had an exhibit filled with the students’ art, and it was simply exceptional; with some …

hostedReviews.name: Friendship Perk & Brew
hostedReviews.text: Friendship Perk & Brew is local coffee shop and sit-down breakfast restaurant has a very homey feel, with some ok java and good pastries.

hostedReviews.name: täkō
hostedReviews.text:
A hip and modern taqueria offering a diversity of elevated tacos in a smaller dark multilevel bar
room. The eponymous Tako taco is their speciality, and while it’s very good, it’s not my favorite.

hostedReviews.name: Gates Center for Computer Science
hostedReviews.location: Gates Center for Computer Science, 5000 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
hostedReviews.text: Built when the Foundation was still called the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the building’s most notable feature is the Guggenheim-esque spiral staircase that oh so slowly snakes down the mainly vertical building.

hostedReviews.name: The Cut
hostedReviews.text: The Cut is the nickname for the central lawn that goes from Forbes Avenue to Hunt Library, including the Fence. I’ve always believed that it’s named that because you need to “cut” across it to get to the other half of the buildings

hostedReviews.name: Walking to the Sky
hostedReviews.text: Walking to the Sky is one of the more prominent artworks on Carnegie Mellon’s campus, maybe second only to The Fence. That being said, I, among many other alums (and I’m sure current day students), really don’t love it.

hostedReviews.name: Google Pittsburgh
hostedReviews.text: When you search “affordable living” on the internal search engine, it sends you to the Pittsburgh office’s page. …

hostedReviews.name: Bakery Square
hostedReviews.text: Bakery Square is a shopping and building complex with a few parking garages, gyms, restaurants and corporate offices. Many of the photos included are from Google Pittsburgh, which is located across two of the buildings here, and includes an employee (and their guest) exclusive cafe.

hostedReviews.name: Steaks West Chester
hostedReviews.location: 698 E Market St Unit 3, West Chester, PA 19382
hostedReviews.text: These folks make a good cheesesteak, the bread was a bit different from what I was expecting, but not in a bad way

hostedReviews.name: Golden Valley Coffee Roasters
hostedReviews.location: 208 Carter Dr Suite 13B, West Chester, PA 19382
hostedReviews.text: They’ve just got a small little store in their larger production building, but they’ve got their beans a-brewing (just a little bit of drip they offered for free), and a ton of varieties to choose from in-house. I’ll definitely be coming back

hostedReviews.name: Ravanesi Pizzeria, Inc.
hostedReviews.text: You need to make a reservation for Ravanesi two weeks in advance, and they ask you how many pizzas you plan to eat that far out. But it’s not hard to see why; they’ve got exceptional pizza dough, which is made into some equally fantastic …

hostedReviews.name: Delaware Border State Sign
hostedReviews.text: Difficult to imagine that Delaware has endless anything, much less discoveries.

hostedReviews.name: Governor Ritchie Scenic Overlook
hostedReviews.text: This is the first opportunity to stop as you’re leaving Annapolis, and while it may be too early for you to be needing a break, it’s a worthwhile stop as you get two attractions in one.

hostedReviews.name: Gold Star Family Monument
hostedReviews.text: While certainly the secondary monument on the hill, the Gold Star Families Memorial is almost the more visually impressive of the two. I love the shadow play of the sculpture.

hostedReviews.name: Maryland World War II Memorial
hostedReviews.text: This Memorial is an impressive visual, on a prominent hillside as you leave Annapolis to go north. The WWII Memorial is a somber site, comprised of an amphitheater of sorts, built up to a star and flags.

hostedReviews.name: Liberty Bell Replica
hostedReviews.text: Situated right at the entrance of St. John’s College, this Liberty Bell is a replica of the original bell before it was cracked, purportedly

hostedReviews.name: Guardians of the First Amendment Memorial
hostedReviews.text: Visiting this one in April 2026 felt especially prescient as we appear to be living through history. It’s funny how things repeat themselves, almost

hostedReviews.name: Kunta Kinte - Alex Haley Memorial
hostedReviews.text: While the statues themselves aren’t the most impressive, I did appreciate the creative arrangement, and the powerful placards scattered around the piers. The memorial is very centrally located in downtown Annapolis, stop for a moment and appreciate it

hostedReviews.name: Mills Fine Wine and Spirits
hostedReviews.text: Quite an expansive wine and spirits store with varietals from all over the world. I like the little maps of all the wine growing regions of each country’s section, and really appreciate that they carry wine and mead.

hostedReviews.name: Reclaimed of Annapolis
hostedReviews.text: An upper-end thrift shop for furniture, much of which has been fixed up since its inception

hostedReviews.name: Annapolis Essentials
hostedReviews.text: If you’re looking to pick up some Old Bay sweatpants on your trip to Maryland, Annapolis Essentials is the place for you. It’s all very touristy, you won’t find anything small and local here.

hostedReviews.name: Back Creek Books
hostedReviews.text: This store has quite the collection of rare and eclectic books. Though the store isn’t especially expansive, there were half a dozen cabinets each with a dozen unique books.

hostedReviews.name: Colonial Annapolis Historic District
hostedReviews.text: Colonial Annapolis is a historic cobblestone area, with a number of notable events in its distant history. Today it’s a lovely shopping area, albeit a bit touristy, with tons of Navy men and women around.

hostedReviews.name: State House Cannon
hostedReviews.text: The cannon looks a bit rough, but it’s had quite the storied history, immortalized with a plaque on it. The thing is mounted on the State House hill, point outwards.

hostedReviews.name: The Annapolis Pottery
hostedReviews.text: An Annapolis institution that I’ve been visiting for my whole life. Rooms upon rooms of every kind of pottery for every use that you can think of, and a few more. If you’re visiting Annapolis for a day trip, perusing this pottery is a must.

hostedReviews.name: Baron Johann de Kalb
hostedReviews.text: Located on the westside of the State House, de Kalb is standing shaking his fist to the sky. He really embodies the great energy of the capitol grounds.

hostedReviews.name: Maryland State House
hostedReviews.text: Annapolis is a town built around a hill by the water, with the State House perched atop the mound. That means that you can see this magnificent building from nearly the whole of Annapolis. In the spring the cherry blossoms really add to the aesthetic. There’s a few statues and a cannon on the grounds

hostedReviews.name: William Preston Lane Jr. Memorial Bay Bridge
hostedReviews.text: The Chesapeake Bay Bridge truly is an impressive bridge to traverse because of its length and various segments with their distinct regions. If you’re afraid of heights, looking around may give you a trippy sensation

hostedReviews.name: Welcome to Maryland sign
hostedReviews.text: It would be annoying to be the person that they left behind, but at least they made the rule afterwards

hostedReviews.name: Buffalo Wild Wings
hostedReviews.text: Large beers and decent wings with a large amount of TVs on every wall playing a variety of sports, what more could you ask for

hostedReviews.name: Passing Through mural

hostedReviews.name: South Station

hostedReviews.name: Kendall/MIT
hostedReviews.text: One of the quirkier T stops that I’ve visited, with a few attractions in the station itself. The Red line stops here

hostedReviews.name: Point Park
hostedReviews.text: The self-proclaimed Most Innovative Square Mile on the Planet, and why not. Who is honestly going to try to prove otherwise

hostedReviews.name: Galaxy Park
hostedReviews.text: A cute little triangular cement park with a globe of sorts in the middle of a fountain. The nicest thing about this very non-green park is the surrounds

hostedReviews.name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston
hostedReviews.text: Stayed here for a work event, and the hotel itself was extremely beautiful, I heard it used to be a jail. My room was in the main building, which seemed to be unique among my coworkers, regardless I really enjoyed my room and my stay.

hostedReviews.name: Viale
hostedReviews.text: A lovely place for dinner that can accommodate large parties. I really enjoyed the oysters, the octopus, and the steak when I came here for a work event.

hostedReviews.name: Google Cambridge

hostedReviews.name: CVS
hostedReviews.text: A fine CVS. They had a decent enough selection, but locking up deodorant is beyond excessive

hostedReviews.name: GetGo Gas Station
hostedReviews.text: A fine enough gas station; the prices weren’t too egregious (all things considered)

hostedReviews.name: Jenny Globe
hostedReviews.text: There aren’t a ton of notable sights as you cross Pennsylvania on the Turnpike, but the Jenny Globe certainly is one of them.

hostedReviews.name: CAVA
hostedReviews.location: 1751 Wilmington Pike Ste B-1, Glen Mills, PA 19342
hostedReviews.text: CAVA is a fast-casual chain which makes middle eastern style food for a reasonable price. I liked the Greek Salad, though the hummus (substituted for tzatziki) wasn’t incredible.

hostedReviews.name: Masamoto Asian Grill & Sushi Bar
hostedReviews.text: Masmoto is a higher end sushi restaurant with a broader array of Asian entrees. We tried a bit of everything, and it was all good! The Sashimi Platter was especially well plated, and all of the fish was extremely fresh. …

hostedReviews.name: Booths Corner Collectibles
hostedReviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
hostedReviews.text: I absolutely love this stand at Booths Corner, these are my go-to movie guys, and it seems like every week they’ve replenished their wares of movies. The best part is that you’re getting them for $1, an unheard of price in America today! You can’t even rent a movie for that low

hostedReviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
hostedReviews.text: There’s an arcade inside of the Booths Corner Farmer’s Market! It’s not incredibly large or fancy, but there’s a small room’s worth of games, including a few pinball games

hostedReviews.name: The Club SFO
hostedReviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, Harvey Milk Terminal 1, International Terminal Departures Level, San Francisco, CA 94128
