hostedReviews.name: San Franpsycho
hostedReviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, HARVEY MILK TERMINAL 1, San Francisco, CA 94128
hostedReviews.text: A local SF brand with fun apparel they make honoring the Bay Area, especially the city. You see them at a lot of neighborhoods’ farmers markets, and now in SFO

hostedReviews.name: Wagon Wheel Barbeque
hostedReviews.text: My rule with barbecue is typically that I don’t eat it unless I can see smoke coming out of the place, and while that wasn’t the case with Wagon Wheel, I did really enjoy all of the things I tried there

hostedReviews.name: Google PLYM1625
hostedReviews.text: There’s a ton of the recent Android OS figurines on the roof of this building (which is only accessible to employees and their guests). I really enjoyed taking a work call of the Android 13 swing.

hostedReviews.name: Concordville Town Centre
hostedReviews.text: A decent little shopping complex with a few restaurants, big box stores, and a bank or two.

hostedReviews.name: Bronze Lyricist - By Bruce Hasson
hostedReviews.location: 1842 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
hostedReviews.text: The statue isn’t too far back from the road, and is quite aesthetically pleasing. It’s unfortunately covered in some rusted bird poop stains

hostedReviews.name: The Orb
hostedReviews.location: 292 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
hostedReviews.text: I can appreciate an abstract piece of art. It’s fun to walk through it and look up at the various openings. At night, the structure is lit up with bright and changing colors

hostedReviews.name: The Ameswell Hotel
hostedReviews.text: My work held a happy hour / dinner event at The Ameswell Hotel, and it was great. The place has a good vibe, and the fire pits were a hot attraction as the sun set. The inside bar is very cool as well

hostedReviews.name: Google Mountain View - Bay View
hostedReviews.location: 100 Bay Vw Dr, Mountain View, CA 94043
hostedReviews.text: One of the newer Googleplex campuses, with a bird’s nest looking building, large security gates, and an exotic interior filled with giant sculptures and newer amenities.

hostedReviews.name: Google Bay View 4
hostedReviews.location: 400 Bay Vw Dr GSuites, Mountain View, CA 94043
hostedReviews.text: These are the Google dorm/hotels, which are only for employees. And while the location is extremely convenient for visiting Googlers going to the eastern portion of the MTV campus, I really didn’t love the rooms themselves

hostedReviews.name: Wells Coffee Tarpon River
hostedReviews.text: Wells Coffee has a delicious drip coffee

hostedReviews.name: MAASS Restaurant at The Four Seasons
hostedReviews.location: 525 N Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33304
hostedReviews.text: MAASS has a Michelin star, and from the moment that you’re seated, you can clearly see why. I had a fantastic brunch here, and while everything was excellent, the pancake was really the standout of the meal. I’ve been thinking about that sweet stack of cakes for much of the last month.

hostedReviews.name: Shell
hostedReviews.text: If you’re headed back to PA, and you have ¾ of a tank or less, stop here and get the cheaper DE gas before you go home

hostedReviews.name: The Shoppes at The Guitar Hotel
hostedReviews.text: There’s a very high-end mall located within the Guitar Hotel is shopping is more of your vice

hostedReviews.name: The Guitar Hotel at Seminole Hard Rock
hostedReviews.text: A visually stunning landmark, and as this hotel is the largest thing in the very flat area, you can see it from miles away. A great place to go for a bit of a walk, whether you’re staying or not

hostedReviews.name: Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino
hostedReviews.text: The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel is such a Fort Lauderdale (area) establishment that you can see the giant guitar and its (2010s 3rd act) skybeam as you land at the airport. …

hostedReviews.name: Las Vegas Cuban Cuisine
hostedReviews.text: Absolutely delicious Cuban food, with really large portions and reasonable prices. I liked my margarita (though there were no choices: frozen or shaken, or flavors), and of all the dishes, I felt that the Yuca fries were the absolute best item we ordered

hostedReviews.name: the seed. Coffee + Juice Bar
hostedReviews.text: A hip coffee shop with an outdoor dining area. I really enjoyed their drip coffee

hostedReviews.name: Beach Pavilion at Lauderdale-By-The-Sea
hostedReviews.text: The aesthetic facade which frames the beach. There’s spots here to sit, in a less sandy spot, and the foot wash stations are here

hostedReviews.name: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Beach
hostedReviews.text: An exceptionally beautiful beach, which wasn’t too crowded and felt like it was largely locals. You do need to park a bit inland and walk down to the shore, but once you’re there, there’s plenty of places to grab lunch, a drink, or some coffee just off the beach

hostedReviews.name: Publix Super Market at Dixie Crossing

hostedReviews.text: They make a decent chicken hoagie, with a ton of fried chicken on it

hostedReviews.name: Fort Lauderdale Fire and Safety Museum, Inc.
hostedReviews.location: 1022 W Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33312
hostedReviews.text: The museum was shut when I walked by in the morning, but I still enjoyed seeing everything the museum has to offer on the exterior

hostedReviews.name: SE 11th Ave Swing Bridge
hostedReviews.text: When in use by cars, the 11th Ave Bridge looks completely normal. But when a ship arrives, the bridge swings itself to get out of the way, a sight to behold

hostedReviews.name: Major William Lauderdale Park
hostedReviews.text: For such a small park, the Major William Lauderdale Park sure does pack a mighty punch. You get not one, but two, plaques, and a fair share of funky faced birds

hostedReviews.name: Sailboat Bend Preserve
hostedReviews.text: The whole grass waterfront portion of Sailboat Bend is just a lovely place to go for a walk and admire the houses and the canal

hostedReviews.name: Flanigan's Seafood Bar and Grill
hostedReviews.text: Flanigan’s is a South Florida staple, and their green plastic cups are iconic to anyone who knows the local chain. Swing by and try the dolphin (not real dolphin meat), or the ribs, or the wings

hostedReviews.name: Cirque du Soleil Luzia Miami
hostedReviews.text: All Cirque du Soleil shows are spectacular, and Luzia was no different! A truly artistic and immersive experience, it was a must see while you’re in the area. All of the performers were excellent

hostedReviews.name: Pegasus and Dragon
hostedReviews.location: 901 S Federal Hwy, Hallandale Beach, FL 33009
hostedReviews.text: A gigantic statue which is brightly lit up at night. You’ll pass by the statue if you’re going to the circus, or the mall complex.

hostedReviews.name: Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens
hostedReviews.location: 253 Barcelona Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33401
hostedReviews.text: Oops, all Picassos! The Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens are a bit of a misnomer, as the terrific sculptures unfortunately can’t hold a candle to all of the Picassos that they’ve accumulated in the house. They’re simply stunning, and they’ve got works across a variety of forms from the famed artist

hostedReviews.name: 7-Eleven
hostedReviews.location: 301 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
hostedReviews.text: What a let down! From the outside, this 7-Eleven is so singular and elevated. But from the inside, there’s nothing special about this, and the fancier area is entirely obscured and you can’t go into the glass room. Don’t bother stopping if the outside beckons

hostedReviews.name: Southern Boulevard Bridge Parking
hostedReviews.text: If you’re trying to get a view of Mar-a-Lago, this is the best place to see it, from across the bay. It’s easiest to get to this parking lot by turning around and heading back from Palm Beach Island

hostedReviews.name: Valen Grounds
hostedReviews.location: 3065 S Dixie Hwy, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
hostedReviews.text: Delicious drip coffee, which was comparatively cheap.

hostedReviews.name: It's All Greek
hostedReviews.location: 522 Belvedere Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
hostedReviews.text: In an extremely pricey neighborhood, It’s All Greek has a wide menu with a variety of reasonably priced dishes. The Greek Salad was large and very fresh, and the chicken was well cooked and flavorful

hostedReviews.name: Isamu Noguchi - Intetra
hostedReviews.text: An interestingly geometric statue which is set at the end of The Four Arts’ avenue, and overlooks West Palm Beach across the short waterway

hostedReviews.name: Garden Club of Palm Beach
hostedReviews.location: 2 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: This was the only portion of The Society of the Four Arts building complex that I was able to explore, and I found these gardens lovely. The area isn’t huge (when the rest of the gardens are shut), but you do get a few unique gardens from around the world to walk around, including a Japanese one.

hostedReviews.name: Philip Hulitar Sculpture Garden
hostedReviews.text: Wasn’t open when I came by, as some private event was being held there later that night. Still, the security people kept changing their rules to stop me from even looking into the main area. What a disappointment the staff here were

hostedReviews.name: The Society of the Four Arts
hostedReviews.location: 100 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: A lovely little aesthetic building, complete with Roman style paintings at the entrance, and an elaborate, worldwide-inspired garden around the back. …

hostedReviews.name: Worth Avenue Clock Tower
hostedReviews.location: 423 S Ocean Blvd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: While the Worth Avenue Clock Tower is quite the simple structure, its location in front of the crystal blue waters makes it quite the spot to take a beautiful photo. Unfortunately, in 2026 this means that you’re going to have a lot of people doing endless, influencer-style photoshoots there.

hostedReviews.name: The Breakers Palm Beach
hostedReviews.location: 1 S County Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: A magnificently stunning hotel, located right on the Atlantic Ocean side of Palm Beach Island. Even if you’re not staying at the hotel, you can explore the grounds and see the impressive building and the lovely beach. You can walk from here to the Flagler museum, directly across the island

hostedReviews.name: Historic Kapok Tree
hostedReviews.location: 315 Chapel Hill Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: Admittedly, even as someone that seldom appreciates trees, this Kapok tree was quite impressive. Almost the starfish of trees, if I may

hostedReviews.name: Flagler Museum
hostedReviews.text: An exceptionally beautiful state home from a generation long gone. This house has everything from elaborate statues to an entire train car inside. When you’re on Palm Beach with some time to spare, visiting the Flagler Museum isn’t a bad way to spend it.

hostedReviews.name: Chik Monk
hostedReviews.location: 229 Sunrise Ave Ste C-5, Palm Beach, FL 33480
hostedReviews.text: The drip coffee was decent, but it felt a bit pricey (that may just be PBI!)

hostedReviews.name: McDonald's
hostedReviews.location: 1630 S Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316
hostedReviews.text: This McDonalds has one of the old school neon signs, with the golden arch.

hostedReviews.name: KUBO Asian fusion and bar -Ft. lauderdale
hostedReviews.text: A Japanese restaurant with very modern designs and stylings, that has some very good sushi. They also do events where they serve an entire tuna, which seems like a true delight

hostedReviews.name: Cooley's Landing Marina
hostedReviews.text: A nice spot to walk around, within the largely Sailboat Bend living area. There’s a plaque to a past tragedy, and an abundance of birds, amongst all of the boats

hostedReviews.location: 1495 SE 17th St D, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316

hostedReviews.text: Not the greatest airport, but this one supports a few areas of southern Florida, from Miami to Palm Beach (though both of those places have their own airports as well). No Priority Pass lounges, but a bunch of character

hostedReviews.text: What a great recent addition to the east bank of the Schuylkill River, which you can see as you drive into Center City on 76.

hostedReviews.name: Stephen's On State
hostedReviews.text: A fine place for dinner! Stephen’s On State has been a staple of State St. for my whole memorable life, but somehow I’ve waited more than 30 years to show up.

hostedReviews.name: Wawa
hostedReviews.text: Not the largest Wawa, but it functions great in a pinch on the way to Philly, and has all the essentials.

hostedReviews.location: Philadelphia International Airport, Terminal D/E, 8500 Essington Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19153
hostedReviews.text: The Chase Sapphire Lounge is a lovely addition to the Philly airport, with its large square footage, fancier food options, and full, complimentary drink menu. …

hostedReviews.name: Tipsy Putt
hostedReviews.text: Came here for a work event, and it was fine. The food wasn’t excellent (Mexican-ish), and the games were fun enough!

hostedReviews.name: Satkar
hostedReviews.location: 1253 W El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087

hostedReviews.text: One of the newest Google buildings, which is inaccessible even to most of the employees who work on the larger Mountain View campus, because of the teams that sit inside

hostedReviews.name: Haze Dispensary
hostedReviews.text: A fine shop, they had a decent supply and a bunch of first time discounts.

hostedReviews.name: Aloft by Marriott Mountain View
hostedReviews.location: 840 E El Camino Real, Mountain View, CA 94040
hostedReviews.text: A nice and convenient place to stay while on a business trip to Mountain View. I was able to check-in at 1:50am without any hassle (I did call ahead and warn that my plane was extremely delayed).

hostedReviews.name: Duck Wall
hostedReviews.text: There are small eccentric pieces of San Francisco which make me love this city, and Duck Wall is absolutely one of them. What wonderful weird art

hostedReviews.name: The Painted Ladies
hostedReviews.text: There’s a good argument to be had about where to find the nicest sunrise in SF, and Alamo Square Park, overlooking The Painted Ladies, must be near the top of any list. You can see the downtown skyscrapers of the Financial District from the park’s perch, and ships beyond in the Bay.

hostedReviews.name: Alamo Square Park
hostedReviews.text: Beautiful views overlooking downtown. The famous Painted Ladies are located on one leg of this park, which features the downtown skyscrapers behind it. Alamo Square Park is a lovely place to take in a sunrise

hostedReviews.name: Sightglass Coffee
hostedReviews.text: Some of the best coffee in the city. Never made a bad drink, and they sell some of my favorite roast beans in the Bay Area

hostedReviews.name: Rock Spinner and Hopscotch
hostedReviews.text: Though this area, at the end of Lawton St, isn’t quite as nice at the Sunset Dunes park area at Newton, there’s still a giant octopus, Lands End mural on the ground, and a truly imposing rock stood upright between the lanes.

hostedReviews.name: Sunset Dunes
hostedReviews.text: I’m so happy that SF voted to transform this portion of the road to a permanent park. It’s a beautiful space along the ocean, open to everyone

hostedReviews.name: Lands End Lookout
hostedReviews.location: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
hostedReviews.text: The area with all the groovy trees above Sutro Baths, which wraps around a good part of the way into the Bay towards the Golden Gate Bridge. hostedReviews.text: This Avis lets you pickup your car directly from the space, if you have Preferred. …

hostedReviews.location: 780 N McDonnell Rd, San Francisco, CA 94128
hostedReviews.text: Apart from being located quite far aware from the airport, the SFO Rental Car Center is quite nice, has a large garage, and a decent variety of companies supported here. …

hostedReviews.name: SFO Museum Gallery Harvey Milk Terminal 1
hostedReviews.location: San Francisco International Airport, 8097, San Francisco, CA 94128
hostedReviews.text: Not the largest gallery space, but there’s a few displays in a dark (and not incredibly inviting) hallway, next to Ritual coffee. It’s worth a quick visit, but certainly not worth risking missing your flight to see

hostedReviews.name: Bun Mee SFO Terminal 3

hostedReviews.text: It’s a really nice looking shop, they’re quite fast, and they’ve got nearly their whole menu from their SF locations. Unfortunately, the food is a hearty step down from the city locations.

hostedReviews.name: San Francisco International Airport
hostedReviews.text: Caveated by this being my home airport, this is absolutely the best airport in the country. Most of the terminals are connected on the inside. If you have TSA Precheck, waits are never longer than 10minutes, and usually only a few people. …

hostedReviews.name: Philadelphia International Airport
hostedReviews.text: While I’m not the biggest fan of PHL, I’ll admit that the airport has gotten quite the facelift in the past few years, and is now about as good as most of the major US airports. …

hostedReviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
hostedReviews.text: A great, reasonably-priced, neighborhood greasy spoon spot for breakfast and lunch eats. The Meat Omelette had a ton of scrapple, and was very hearty for the price - the Home Fries were likewise great. The only downside is that breakfast ends at 1pm.

hostedReviews.name: Dos Gringos Mexican Kitchen
hostedReviews.text: I enjoyed the Tacos Mexicanos with Pork Carnitas from Dos Gringos. If you dine-in, they give you some warm, fresh (tasting) tortilla chips and salsa, and the verde was mild but nicely flavorful. …

hostedReviews.name: La Buona Cucina
hostedReviews.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
hostedReviews.text: Delicious prepackaged Italian meals, which you can freeze to make last longer.

hostedReviews.name: AMC Lincoln Square 13
hostedReviews.text: I’ve seen movies in a dozen states, and this has to be the coolest theatre that I’ve ever seen! On the second floor, the hallway and each theatre has been uniquely designed to reflect something related to film, Hollywood, or movie theatres. …

hostedReviews.name: Dante West Village
hostedReviews.text: I came to Dante with a party of 20 for a large work event, and they had customized the menu for us, which was pretty unique and a very nice touch. Then the food was absolutely delicious, the chicken was so well cooked, but really everything …

hostedReviews.name: M&M'S New York
hostedReviews.text: The M&M store in Times Square is something of a tourist attraction, as there’s mascots, apparel, and signage recognizing the prominent location, but if you’re not trying to buy some chocolate or a souvenir, there’s little to see or do

hostedReviews.name: Chelsea Market
hostedReviews.text: A block-long food market with a wide variety of permanent vendors, and a mix of other shops. There’s often some cool displays detailing older NYC of years past, and to the history of the building, which was once a biscuit factory.

hostedReviews.name: Grand Bazaar NYC
hostedReviews.text: A weekly market with dozens of vendors arranged in a tennis court, expanding into a high school gymnasium. There were mainly clothing, goods, and art stands, with a food section by the entrance and free Vitamin Water samples.

hostedReviews.name: The Viand
hostedReviews.text: While The Viand isn’t an old-school NYC diner, they still get the job done when you’re in need of a breakfast. They’ve got quite large omelettes for a fair price, which come with homemade jam. The coffee was fine

hostedReviews.name: Gray's Papaya
hostedReviews.text:
Gray’s Papaya is an institution of the Upper West
Side, most notably for their hot dogs and their papaya juice, but they also sell quite tasty breakfast sandwiches which are only $3 with a cup of coffee. …

hostedReviews.name: AMC 84th Street 6
hostedReviews.text: One of the smaller AMC theatres in the city, and while they don’t have any larger format screens here (no IMAX or Dolby), they do have the fancy recliners; so you get comfort over the visual resolution.

hostedReviews.name: 7th Street Burger Upper West Side
hostedReviews.text: A good place to stop and get a good, greasy smash burger and some fries. The burgers were better than the fries, and same as with Five Guys, you’ll likely want to get a double if you’re an adult. …

hostedReviews.text: A great option for a lunch on the go. The salads were reasonably priced and extremely portable. I’d definitely recommend the Greek Salad and adding Chicken, you also get free bread.

hostedReviews.name: The Met Cloisters
hostedReviews.location: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
hostedReviews.text: The Met Cloisters is situated atop a hill at the very tippy top of Manhattan, and serves as something of a prize for venturing up to the sleepier portion of the island. …

hostedReviews.name: Citi Field
hostedReviews.text: Citi Field is home of the New York Mets, and they also use the stadium for some corporate events and concerts. It’s a great venue with a good variety of vendors. …

hostedReviews.name: Superfly New York City - Upper West Side Licensed Adult-Use Recreational Dispensary
hostedReviews.text: A decent dispensary with a wide selection, and a slightly higher price point. It looks fancy inside, and they’ve got machines where you can view their products.

hostedReviews.name: The Strand
hostedReviews.text: Some book stores have this calming ambiance and The Strand has that in heaps. An extremely expansive bookstore with a children’s section in the basement.

hostedReviews.text: An extremely densely packed hardware store that’s likely got what you’re looking for. There were a number of employees ready to help me as well.

hostedReviews.name: Crumbl Cookies
hostedReviews.text: The national gourmet, giant cookie and cake chain. Their desserts are good, but certainly more of a treat, or a gift, than a regular item. …

hostedReviews.name: Moynihan Food Hall
hostedReviews.text: The Moynihan Food Hall (within Penn Station) has a surprisingly wide selection of restaurants to choose from before you catch your train.

hostedReviews.text: 7 Hudson Square is the new home of Disney in New York, both the corporate offices, and the studio spaces living within the building. In the mornings, you can see celebrities entering and exiting the building for their media obligations, and upstairs there’s a theatre for employee only screenings, and a Starbucks

hostedReviews.name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir
hostedReviews.text: The Reservoir is the largest body of water in Central Park and one of its most notable landmarks. You can’t go out onto the water, and you certainly can’t swim in it. There is a running track that goes along the perimeter of the body of water, which enforces a single direction of traffic, counter-clockwise.

hostedReviews.name: The Lake
hostedReviews.location: Central Park, Bow Bridge, New York, NY 10024
hostedReviews.text: There’s a few bodies of water within Central Park and The Lake is one of the more prominent ones, although not the largest. But for The Pond, it’s the most downtown body of water, so it gives some of the best reflected skyscraper views. You can also see the Dakota and other iconic UWS buildings from here.

hostedReviews.name: St. Paul the Apostle Church
hostedReviews.text: New York City has no shortage of beautiful churches, but St. Paul the Apostle stands out in that crowded field. Not only does it have a brilliant facade, it has a stunningly colorful, cavernous interior. I could’ve spent hours here studying every detail, this building is truly a work of art.

hostedReviews.name: Swingers NoMad
hostedReviews.text: A very expansive, indoor miniature golf place, with multiple courses located on the property. It’s a very aesthetically pleasing place, with colorful lights, and good scenes for photography. They also have decent food and drinks. I came here for a work event and we all had a great time

hostedReviews.name: Imagine Mosaic
hostedReviews.location: Imagine, Terrace Dr, New York, NY 10023
hostedReviews.text: The Upper West Side has its own little, micro Times Square in the former of a tribute to a former Beatle. This is one of the few, rare places that you’ll spot a crowd in the quieter neighborhood, and plenty of vendors hocking their wares, and musicians busking famous Lennon tracks.

hostedReviews.name: Times Square Diner & Grill
hostedReviews.text: I was trying to get brunch somewhere else in the neighborhood, but they were crowded, so I came to the Times Square Diner and they were fine. The Strawberry Nutella Pancakes were really the standout, with the omelettes and home fries both just being fine. I didn’t love the coffee.

hostedReviews.name: Peace Fountain by Greg Wyatt
hostedReviews.text: The Peace Fountain may be my singular favorite statue in the whole of New York City. There’s so much going on, it’s chaotic, it’s messy, it’s fantastic. It’s surrounded by a ring of smaller animal statues, complimenting the animal parts that encompass the larger artwork.

hostedReviews.name: H&H Bagels
hostedReviews.location: Moynihan Train Hall, 421 8th Ave, New York, NY 10199
hostedReviews.text: The H&H in Penn Station is located between the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall and the Food Court, and while there’s often a line, it does move quickly. This is a fair place to grab a breakfast before heading on your train, or a black and white cookie as a gift.

hostedReviews.name: City Diner
hostedReviews.text: A large square-footage diner with a bar counter, an old timey feel, and some good pancakes. A friend and I got two Egg dishes (an Omelette and Eggs), and an order of Chocolate Chip Pancakes, and the cakes were by far the standout. Also didn’t love the house coffee.

hostedReviews.name: Tom's Restaurant
hostedReviews.text: Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent

hostedReviews.name: Kossar's Bagels & Bialys
hostedReviews.text: Kossar’s makes an excellent breakfast sandwich, I went with my typical Sausage, Egg, and Cheese on an Everything Bagel, and I loved what I got. They brew La Colombe coffee, and my only complaint is that their cups are horrible; it still leaked through two cups

hostedReviews.name: Hall of Saurischian Dinosaurs
hostedReviews.text: One of my favorite parts of the History Museum, filled with Dinosaurs stretching across vast halls, and towering over crowds. But be wary, this is also one of the busiest parts of the building, with a heavy density of people filling every nook and cranny.

hostedReviews.name: Horace Greeley Monument
hostedReviews.location: 894-900 Ave Of The Amer, New York, NY 10001
hostedReviews.text: Horace has the misfortune of having both an old looking face and an old sounding name. At least they gave the old guy a chair to spend eternity in. They’ve also surrendered him with flowers, making the whole thing look almost like a tomb. RIP Ol’ Horace

hostedReviews.name: Carl Schurz Park
hostedReviews.location: East 86th Street &, East End Ave, New York, NY 10028
hostedReviews.text: Carl Schurz Park is located on the East River in the Upper East Side, and contains a section of John Finley walk and Gracie Mansion. There’s also a Peter Pan Statue and a lot of green shrubbery, it’s a fine place to go for a break or a bit of a walk.

hostedReviews.name: Penn Station
hostedReviews.text: NY Penn Station has a worse reputation than it deserves. As someone that regularly uses Amtrak, I really like the aesthetic design of the station, the availability of the subways underneath, and the selection of restaurants and shops and their hours.

hostedReviews.name: Schmackary's
hostedReviews.text: Somehow NYC has a bunch of competing gourmet cookie chains. Schmackary’s is a delicious offering, with more reasonably sized cookies, which were all named after Broadway shows. I got the Book of Mormon one, which was great. I’ll be back to try more.

hostedReviews.name: The Ravine
hostedReviews.text: There’s a few areas of Central Park where you can get deep enough into the green to forget that you’re still in the heart of the largest city in the country. The Ravine is one of those places, which makes it one of my favorite parts of the megacity

hostedReviews.name: Eleanor Roosevelt Memorial
hostedReviews.text: Eleanor Roosevelt was the first female aviatrix to fly across the Pacific Ocean, until everything changed when she vanished one day from her house never to be seen again. People have searched everywhere for her plane, but no one knows where it went

hostedReviews.name: Läderach
hostedReviews.text: A gourmet chocolatier with a higher price point which makes decent gifts for loved ones. The store has a human-sized statue of liberty made out of chocolate inside, and heaps of sheets of chocolate. They also tend to give out free samples as well.

hostedReviews.name: Sutton Park
hostedReviews.text: There’s really three attractions in Sutton Park, first the stunning views of the Queensboro Bridge. Then there’s quite a nice statue to a boar in a greener portion of the park. And finally, there’s the views of the Eastern portions of the city.

hostedReviews.name: Morningside Park
hostedReviews.text: While not as famous as Central Park or Riverside Park, Morningside Park is one of Manhattans great parks. Located above Central Park on the westside, this park offers a number of steep, hilly paths, and a serene lake with a purported waterfall.

hostedReviews.name: Times Square
hostedReviews.text: Times Square is arguably the most famous place in New York City, and in turn, maybe the most consistently busy. There’s a ton to see, from people watching, to taking in the thousands of neon adverts blaring, there’s much to see in Times Square

hostedReviews.name: Apthorp Cleaners
hostedReviews.text: Apthorp Cleaners have some of the most elaborate storefront windows that I’ve seen on the UWS. The current two are Barbie and Wicked: For Good, and there’s easily a dozen dolls in each with custom backgrounds and floors, arranged into scenes.

hostedReviews.name: Porto Rico Importing Co.
hostedReviews.text: One of the best smelling shops in NYC, with endless burlap sacks full of roast coffee beans, and their beans are largely quite good. There’s staff that can walk you through choosing the right beans for your tastes, and they also have all of …

hostedReviews.name: Central Park
hostedReviews.text: NYC’s iconic park, and one of the largest urban parks in the world, Central Park is the home to multiple bodies of water, horse stables, and fantastic views of the large residential buildings that line the sides, and skyscrapers at its base.

hostedReviews.name: Inwood Hill Park
hostedReviews.location: Payson Ave. &, Seaman Ave, New York, NY 10034
hostedReviews.text: If you’re looking for the furthest north point in Manhattan, you’ve found it! Inwood Hill Park sits at the northwest corner of the island, and is equally dense with trees and sparse with humans (on the ground). Though you can nearly always …

hostedReviews.name: Gracie Mansion Conservancy
hostedReviews.location: 181 East End Ave, New York, NY 10128
hostedReviews.text: Honestly, I didn’t realize that Gracie Mansion was located here when I was intending to see Peter Pan, but this was something of a nice surprise. You really can’t get up close to the building at all, which makes sense, for security purposes.

hostedReviews.name: Carnegie Hall
hostedReviews.location: 57th Street and, 7th Ave, New York, NY 10019
hostedReviews.text: Carnegie Hall is one of the preeminent concert venues in the country, if not the world, and you can almost feel the grandeur in the halls. I was lucky enough to see Gustavo Dudamel conduct Tosca here, and will certainly try to return soon

hostedReviews.name: Google NYC - Chelsea Market
hostedReviews.text: Google purchased the entirety of the historic Chelsea Market building more than a decade ago, and while the public floors haven’t been updated, the upper (employee only) floors are really quite exquisite, and one of the more interesting …

hostedReviews.name: Bareburger
hostedReviews.text: I really enjoyed Bareburger, they’re a slightly more elevated NYC burger chain, with a bit of a higher price point, which gets you a higher quality burger, with more fun accoutrements. It’s also a sit down restaurant, which caught me by …

hostedReviews.name: Non-Violence - Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd
hostedReviews.location: United Nations Secretariat Building, 405 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017
hostedReviews.text: I’m certain Non-Violence is a better statue than I’ve reviewed it, but it’s so inaccessible from the street, it’s a true shame. Art shouldn’t be hidden behind walls, and I’d assume the UN (of all organizations) that should understand that

hostedReviews.name: Just Salad
hostedReviews.text: Great salads, and they come with free rosemary-y bread. They have a whole array of precurated options, and you can swap out any ingredients that you want. Just Salad also has a rewards program in you get their app, or go on the website. …

hostedReviews.name: 190 St
hostedReviews.text: Quite an interesting metro station. The signage at the upper level is cool and retro, however you have to take an elevator down from there. There’s another entrance, at the ground level, but no stairs or escalators to get you down there

hostedReviews.name: Mount Tom
hostedReviews.text: Less of a mountain and more of a big honking rock, you can climb Mount Tom and get a decent overview of the Warsaw Monument, but on account of the heavy tree cover, not much else. Still, it’s a fun place to do a bit of rock scrambling.

hostedReviews.name: Church of the Heavenly Rest
hostedReviews.text: An exceptionally stunning single-halled church. Cast with white stone calls, and elaborate stained glass panels lining three of the side, the Church of the Heavenly Rest exudes beauty from every pew and from under each and every arch.

hostedReviews.name: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine
hostedReviews.location: 701 Fort Washington Ave, New York, NY 10040
hostedReviews.text: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine is a church, so if you’re visiting on a Sunday, there will be services going on. There was a front area with a gift shop-appearing section, that was cool even if I didn’t get to see the rest of the building

hostedReviews.name: General Grant National Memorial
hostedReviews.location: W 122nd St &, Riverside Dr, New York, NY 10027
hostedReviews.text: The General Grant Memorial has a few unique things going for it. Maybe most notable is the mosaic bench that stretches around the perimeter of the building. Closely followed by Grant’s tomb which is just a bit north of the building.

hostedReviews.name: American Museum of Natural History
hostedReviews.location: 200 Central Prk W, New York, NY 10024
hostedReviews.text: Certainly one of the best Natural History Museums in the country, if not the world. Regardless of which animal, vegetable, or mineral you’re hoping to see, it’s likely in this museum. My favorite exhibits were the butterflies, the …

hostedReviews.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
hostedReviews.text: When you’re in Penn Station and need a quick cup of coffee, or a pastry, Blue Bottle isn’t a bad option. They’re situated right in the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall, which is super convenient for those commuting via train.
